title: Περὶ ῥηματικῶν ὀνομάτων
author: Herodian (grammarian)

passages.original: Πῖϲα παρὰ τὸν πίϲω μέλλοντα, οὗ ἡ χρῆϲιϲ παρὰ Πινδάρῳ. Πίνδαροϲ δὲ κατὰ ϲυϲτολὴν τὴν πόλιν εἶπε Πίϲαν.
passages.english: Pisa [is formed] from the future *pisō* ["I shall give to drink"], the use of which is found in Pindar. And Pindar called the city Pisa with a shortened [vowel].
passages.notes: The future *pisō* belongs to the poetic verb *pipiskō* "give to drink". The second sentence presumably contrasts Pindar's short iota in *Pisa* with the long iota implied by the derivation, but the text does not make the point explicit.

passages.original: τὸ κνύζα ἐπὶ τοῦ παρεφθαρμένου καὶ ἐρρυπωμένου ἀπὸ τοῦ κνύω, ἀφ’ οὗ κνύοϲ ἡ φθορά οἰον «κατὰ κνύοϲ ἔχευεν, ψίλωτο δὲ — κάρηνα» (Ηes. frg. XL II) γίνεται ὡϲ παρ’ Ἀνακρέοντι «κνύζη τιϲ ἤδη καὶ πέπειρα γενομένη ϲὴν διὰ μαργοϲύνην ».
passages.english: The [word] *knyza* [is used] of what is spoiled and soiled, from *knyō*, from which [comes] *knyos*, 'decay', as in "he poured down decay, and [the] heads were stripped bare" (Hesiod, fragment 40.2). It occurs as in Anacreon: "someone already *knyzē* [withered] and become ripe, [...] through lust".
passages.notes: The author 'xtlg0087' is unidentified; it may be the TLG number for Herodian (On Verbal Nouns). In the Hesiod quotation the dash marks an omitted word before κάρηνα, probably 'all'. The Anacreon fragment is corrupt as transmitted. The phrase ϲὴν διὰ μαργοϲύνην makes poor sense, perhaps 'your [...] through lust'. I have left ϲὴν untranslated and marked it [...]. 'Withered' for κνύζη is a conjectural gloss.

passages.original: κνύοϲ ἡ φθορά παρὰ τὸ κνύω παρ’ Ἡϲιόδῳ ὡϲ παρὰ τὸ θύω θύοϲ καὶ φλύω φλύοϲ παρὰ Ἀρχιλόχῳ ἐπὶ φλυαρίαϲ.
passages.english: *Knyos*, 'decay', [is formed] from *knyō* in Hesiod, just as *thyos* [comes] from *thyō*, and *phlyos* from *phlyō*, [used] in Archilochus for 'babbling'.
